summary: Astronauts from many countries live and work on the International Space Station, adapting to floating in space while doing science.
introduce: Write the key term “orbit” on the board and give pairs thirty seconds to guess what it means. Share a few guesses, then tell students to find the word in “Living in Space: The International Space Station” and check whether they were right.

keyTerms.def: the curved path an object follows as it travels around a planet, moon, or star
a condition in space where people and things feel almost weightless and float
to clean or change something that has been used so it can be used again

challengeTerms.def: one section of a larger structure that can be joined to other sections
having had the water removed, often to make food last longer

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that living on a space station would be more exciting than difficult? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Choose one challenge of living in microgravity.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review orbit, microgravity, and recycle, and let weak readers draw a quick picture for each term and use it in a short spoken sentence.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use module, dehydrated, and continuously in a short paragraph that teaches the class one of the terms with their own example.
